claims.text: A tailored surface modification can form a continuous spinel oxide coating on a high-entropy alloy.
A continuous spinel oxide coating will reduce combined high-temperature tribo-corrosion degradation relative to an untreated HEA.
The initial HEA has a homogeneous microstructure.
Laser cladding or controlled oxidation can promote in situ formation of a continuous protective spinel oxide layer.
The engineered spinel oxide layer acts as a self-healing barrier.
The spinel oxide layer provides a hard and stable interface that reduces mechanical wear.
The spinel oxide layer limits chemical interaction and thereby reduces corrosive attack.
The surface-engineered HEA will show a statistically significant reduction in wear depth relative to an untreated HEA.
The surface-engineered HEA will show a statistically significant reduction in corrosion weight loss relative to an untreated HEA.
Performance may vary when oxide formation is not sufficiently controlled.
Performance may deteriorate when service conditions exceed the stability limits of the oxide layer.
Oxide-layer adhesion, long-term phase stability, and local testing conditions may affect the magnitude of improvement.
